_fixture_notes.label: player_names_and_trend_form
_fixture_notes.scenario: A Red Sox win in the production boxscore shape, where every player name in the data is a BARE LAST NAME ("Tolle", "Chapman") the way MLB's boxscoreName hands them over. CURRENT_ROSTER carries the full names. This is the September 2026 regression: the fetcher fix now sends fullName, but the persona must still resolve a bare last name from the roster rather than shipping it, and must spend those full names the way a writer does.
_fixture_notes.why_this_exists: Every other fixture hand-writes full names, so none of them exercised the resolution path or the trend-field format. The published 2026-09-07 post opened "Tolle was absolute nails on the mound" and set trend to "6.0 innings, 12 strikeouts, 1 earned run".
pass_criteria: trend_watch[].player is a full first-and-last name on EVERY entry ("Payton Tolle", not "Tolle")
trend_watch[].trend is one complete sentence carrying the stats ("Struck out twelve over six innings and gave up a single earned run.")
trend_watch[].trend does not open with a digit and contains no em dash
In morning_brew, each player's FIRST appearance is the full name
In morning_brew, LATER appearances of that same player are last name / nickname / pronoun, not the full name again
The three-reliever run reads naturally as bare last names in one clause ("Miller, Moran, and Chapman"), not as three full names in a row
fail_criteria: Any bare last name in a trend_watch player field
trend set to a comma-joined stat line ("6.0 innings, 12 strikeouts, 1 earned run")
A body that never introduces anyone by full name (the pre-fix failure)
A body that repeats the full name on every mention (the over-correction: reads like a press release)
"LastName, Initial" format anywhere in the output
_fixture_notes.review: Manual, per eval_voice.py — the interesting failure is the middle ground, so read the runs rather than grepping for one full name and calling it green. Run n=3: the body rule is a judgement call the model can get right once by luck.
